quizName: DMV Practice Test #13 40 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful. It provides at least 70 percent of a motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, how should the following distance change?
questions.explanation: You should increase your following distance when towing a trailer. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What should be part of your normal scanning routine while riding?

options.text: Constantly looking in the rearview mirror.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently while riding. Also check them before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, which part of your lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This gives you a better view and helps other drivers see your passing move.

questions.question: If you are carrying a passenger, what should they do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you through turns and curves. They should sit as far forward as possible without interfering with your control, and hold onto passenger handholds or your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders be positioned?
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should be positioned just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them from behind.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Which action will NOT help you maintain control in a turn?
questions.explanation: To control your motorcycle in a turn, slow down before entering the turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go, lean the motorcycle by pressing the handle grip, and gently increase throttle through the turn.

questions.question: What is true about convex mirrors?

options.text: They provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
They provide a wide view of the road behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: They provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. However, objects appear farther away than they actually are. Get used to your mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing your motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stop until the animal loses interest.

questions.explanation: Downshift and slowly approach the dog. Once you are close, accelerate and leave it behind. Do not try to kick the dog.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when being passed. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to pull back into your lane too quickly.

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Turn by using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Lean your motorcycle in the direction of the turn. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: While riding, you should wear:

options.text: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
A helmet to protect your hearing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hearing protection to prevent damage from engine and wind noise.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a full-face helmet. Wear hearing protection to prevent this damage.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, what is the minimum safe following distance?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between your motorcycle and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a potential hazard?

options.text: Road conditions that stay the same as you approach.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions that stay the same as you approach.
questions.explanation: Watch for hazards on the road and have a plan to avoid them. Conditions that don't change are not hazardous.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A yellow light warns that the signal will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection, continue through it.

questions.question: When riding behind a car in the center portion of the lane:

options.text: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
The driver usually cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane behind a car so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position is safest.

questions.question: A helmet provides the most protection if it has all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: A helmet should meet U.S. Department of Transportation standards, fit snugly, and have no cracks or damage. A loose-fitting helmet does not provide good protection.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, where should you ride?

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the center portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle risks a collision. Riding on the far side may cause the driver to return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should instruct them to:

options.text: Get on before you start the engine.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell passengers not to talk or move while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should only board after the engine has started. They should sit as far forward as possible without interfering with you.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help reduce serious injury in a crash?
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather jacket or sturdy synthetic material also protects against injury. A sweatshirt does not provide the same protection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This regulatory sign has white background with red and black markings. It tells drivers what traffic laws apply in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift immediately to a lower gear.
Proceed in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over uneven gratings, stay relaxed and continue straight at a steady speed. Steering in a zigzag pattern is more dangerous than the weaving.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down to watch for changes in the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over grooved pavement.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
It knows when to brake automatically by understanding your riding habits.
It is connected to the gears and applies the brake when downshifting.

questions.correctAnswerText: It links the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is applied.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that connect the front and rear brakes. When you use the rear brake pedal, both brakes work together. Check your owner's manual to learn about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield alone is not enough protection.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Be ready to act to avoid a hazard.
Turn your headlight off during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your headlight off during the day.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to other drivers. Use your signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and always scan ahead, behind, and beside your bike.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, it is usually best to:

options.text: Use the shoulder of the road to slow down before crossing the tracks.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: It is safest to ride straight within your lane when crossing angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your path angle may move you into another lane and cause a collision.

questions.question: Hearing protection:

options.text: Is not needed when the rider is wearing a helmet.
Is only recommended for long trips.
Should be used on all rides.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used on all rides.
questions.explanation: Engine and wind noise can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection on all rides.

questions.question: If your motorcycle begins to wobble, you should:

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Do not accelerate out of a wobble. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble, slowly close the throttle to slow down, and lean forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as you safely can.

questions.question: What is true about a windshield?

options.text: It works as well as a face shield.
It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
It is required on all motorcycles.
You should use it only on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield does not protect your eyes like goggles or a face shield do. Most windshields will not keep wind out of your eyes.

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
Where you can see best and be seen by others.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where you can see best and be seen by others.
questions.explanation: When entering a curve, move to the best position to see and be seen. For a left curve, stay right to spot oncoming traffic early. For a right curve, stay left to see ahead without getting too close to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that traffic ahead will be merging.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you are about to slow down quickly.
When a stop sign is ahead.
When your turn signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are about to slow down quickly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly, especially if a driver is following too closely. They may not see hazards ahead that you do.

questions.question: Why should a rider change gears before turning?

options.text: To avoid sudden power changes during the turn.
So both hands stay on the handlebars.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid sudden power changes during the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start turning. Shifting while turning can cause sudden power changes that make the rear wheel skid. If you must shift in a turn, do it smoothly.

questions.question: What causes an engine to seize?
questions.explanation: An engine seizes when it runs low on oil. Without oil, the engine's parts cannot move smoothly and the engine overheats.

questions.question: What should you do when riding over rough pavement in a work zone?

options.text: Look down at the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Stay to the left side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up on rough pavement. Ride slowly, keep your throttle steady, and do not fight the handlebars.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black symbols. This sign warns you that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is displayed on the back of slow-moving vehicles like construction equipment, farm machinery, or horse-drawn vehicles that travel slower than 25 mph.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time they ride. A helmet is your best protection against head and neck injuries in an accident.
